lessonSteps.text: Congratulations! You have got the Code & Movement Robotics Field Lab
Open the box
Find these parts that will be used for building the platform
We will start with mounting the motor driver
Start by taking one brass standoff and a short 3mm screw
Insert the screw from the lower part of the base plate
Then, attach the standoff to it from the upper part of the base plate
...Like so
Screw it in and tighten
Repeat for the following 4 holes
Now place the motor driver like so
Attach it to the base plate using a short 3mm screws
Then, repeat for all 4 holes
...Like so
Take the I/O Shield
Start preparing standoffs for it, too
Use these 4 holes
Then, mount the I/O shield to the base plate using 4 short 3mm screws
...Line so
Next, attach 2 more standoffs for the MPU6050 Accelerometer
...Using these holes
Next, mount the accelerometer
...Like so
Install the ESP8266 Mictocontroller board onto the I/O shield
And press it in, like so
Next, take the reflectance sensor, the long bras standoff and a short 3mm screw
Attach the standoff to the sensor using the screw
And tighten, like so
Place the sensor on the base plate like so
And mount, using another short 3mm screw
Make sure that the sensor can "see" the ground via the hole
Your board should now look like this
Next, take the 2 motors, 4 motor mounts, 2 wheels and the bag containing long screws
Start by inserting the motor mount from the back side of the base plate
Then, push it in all the way
Repeat for the second side
The front side of your base plate should now look like this

Place one of the motors next to the motor mont. 
*** Mind the motor orientation ***
Place the second motor mount like so, in the groove prepared for it in the base plate
Take a long screw and place it in through the hole
Push it all the way in, rocking gently if needed. Do not use force or the wood might break!
Make sure it exists from the other side, like so
Add a washer onto the screw
And secure with a nut
Use a screwdriver to tighten, but leave some play
Insert the second screw
Again, make sure it exists from the other side
Add a washer
And secure with a nut
Tighten both screws to the maximum, without damaging the wood
Mount the back plate into the base plate using the groove and the hole
Pass motor wires through the designated holes, like so
Start unscrewing the motor driver connection blocks in an anti-clockwise motion, about 3-4 turns each
This one, too
And this
Go through all screws
Open all of them
...Like so
One more to go!
Next, insert the black wire coming from onw of the motors into the appropriate hole in the motor driver at the corresponding side. Mind the color and the target location of the wire
Attach the wire to the connection block using the screw. Make sure that the wire stays in place when gently tugged
Now insert the red wire. Again, make sure the wires are connected into the same locations as in the photos.
Screw this connection block, too
Now, do the other side. Make sure the wire location is the same as in the photo
...And tighten
Last one, red wire of the second motor
...And tighten
Your base plate should now look like this
the the switch and attached wires
Place the black wires soldered together into the middle connection block on the motor driver
...Yes, this one
And screw it in until connection it stable
Thake the red wire coming from the black connection socket and connect it to the connection terminal in the picture
Tighten its screw
Take the red wire coming from the switch and insert it to the last hole. Make sure it is the same hole as in the picture!
And tighten its screw
Connect the microcontroller power supply to the I/O shield. Mind the direction / polarity of the connection!
Take 4 wires from the colorful female-to-female wire band and separate it
Connect the 4 wires to the motor driver according to the photo
Connect the other end of the 4 wires to the I/O shield according to the photo
Tuck the wire under the board so that it does not stick out
Now, take 3 wires from the colorful female-to-female wire band and separate it
Connect the 3 wires to the reflectance sensor according to the photo
Connect the other end of the 3 wires to the I/O shield according to the photo
Bend the sensor's connection terminals like so
Until the wires are pointing upwards
Again, tuck the wire in so that it does not get tangled in anything else
Now, take 4 wires from the colorful female-to-female wire band and separate it
Connect the 4 wires to the accelerometer according to the photo
Connect the other end of the 4 wires to the I/O shield according to the photo
Tuck this wire, too. Almost done with the wiring!
Locate the buzzer
And connect it to pin D8, as in the photo
Time for batteries! find the 8 batteries and the battery compartment
Insert the batteries into the compartment
Take a double sided adhesive tape
Peel one of its sides
Attach to the battery compartment
...Like so
Peel the other side of the tape
And attach at the 'Battery Compartment' marking on the base plate
Attach the battery connector to the battery compartment
...Like so
Next, turn the robot on using the switch
Make sure these 3 lights get turned on (and no smoke coming up! hahaha)
Next, mount wheels onto the motor shaft
Like so
Make sure the wheel does not touch the screw
Repeat for the second wheel and motor
Locate the 2 side plates
Place one of them at the side of the robot, making sure the writing is turned outside
Press it in, gently
Repeat for the second side
Like so
Take the front plate, the laser sensor, a small bag of 2mm screws and the remaining wires
Take 4 wires from the colorful female-to-female wire band and separate it
Connect the 4 wires to the laser sensor according to the photo
Insert one 2mm screw to the sensor, like so
Gently push it all the way in
Add a nut on the other side
And screw it in, gently
Repeat for the second hole, like so
Now insert 2 washers onto the screws
Insert the wires through the designated hole in the front plate
...Like so
Insert the other 2 washers onto the front plate
And secure with 2mm nuts
This is how it should look like
attach the front plate in place
Slightly lifting the side plates to connect to it
...Like so
And from the other side, too
...Like so
Until everything is in place
Connect the wires coming from the laser sensor to the I/O shield, as in the photo
Take the top plate
Slide the switch wires through the wire channel
Place the switch into the hole  prepared for it
And gently squeeze, to secire
Take the USB cable
insert in into the robot through the hole in the back plate
And connect to the microcontroller. You may find it easier to first release the microcontroller from its socket, then place it back into its place
Place the top plate in place and gently squeeze it into place
Go gradually, one hole at a time
Until The top is firmly in place
Last step! locate the 2 acrylic pieces
intertwine them one into the other
...Like so
All the way
It should be level
and place it against the base plate's bottom side, matching the holes
Press the acrylic into the base plate, one hole at a time. this should be a tight fit, so do not use force just gradually wiggle each of the holes until the piece slides in
This is how it should look like
Finally, take the hood with 2 zip ties
Insert the zip ties into the side holes in the hood
And then through the corresponding hole in the top plate
Pull the zip tie almost until the end
Repeat on the other side
And tighten
...Like so
Cut the excess zip tie
...And here, too

Ta-Dah! 
You are done, CONGRATULATIONS!
